title: 2026-09-11 Research Notes — Cross-Theory Scientific Upgrade Program
novelty_scope: Novel as a project architecture added on 2026-09-11; the scientific methods it imports are established methods and are not claimed as globally novel.
core_finding: The science corpus is now large enough that its next gains are less likely to come from adding isolated equations and more likely to come from forcing every theory through the same research contract: type variables, remove units by nondimensionalization where possible, state symmetries/invariants, establish identifiability, define observables, compare baselines, and record failure conditions.

new_project_rules.proposal: Represent cross-domain models as typed blocks rather than one undifferentiated state vector.
new_project_rules.equation: X=(X_phys, X_bio, X_neuro, X_info, X_graph, X_archive, X_symbolic)
new_project_rules.rule: A coupling C_ab is legal only when a map from the units/types of block a to block b is explicitly declared. Symbolic similarity alone does not create a scientific coupling.

new_project_rules.proposal: Before comparing equations across physical or biological domains, convert each concrete model to dimensionless variables and identify the controlling dimensionless groups.
new_project_rules.finding: Two systems that look symbolically similar become scientifically comparable only if their dimensionless dynamics or invariants also align.

new_project_rules.proposal: Every claimed invariant should name the transformation under which it is invariant.
examples: time-translation symmetry -> energy conservation only when the action and assumptions support Noether's theorem
rotation symmetry -> angular-momentum structure in the appropriate physical model
Door transition -> project-specific invariant only if D preserves a declared quantity
new_project_rules.finding: This prevents the archive from calling a repeated motif an invariant merely because it reappears.

questions: Can distinct parameter values produce identical observables?
Can distinct source/channel decompositions produce identical outputs?
Which transformations leave the likelihood unchanged?
Which new intervention would break the degeneracy?
new_project_rules.finding: A mathematically elegant model can be empirically meaningless if its important parameters cannot in principle be distinguished.

new_project_rules.proposal: Every richer model must pay for extra parameters by improving prediction or compression relative to a simpler baseline.
new_project_rules.finding: This is especially important for Spiral, 11D, consciousness and celestial models because flexible geometry can fit patterns after the fact.

new_project_rules.proposal: A relationship edge is not automatically causal. Promote a causal edge only with temporal ordering plus intervention, natural experiment, mechanistic evidence or a defensible causal design.
new_project_rules.finding: This strengthens both the science corpus and the wider relational atlas because it separates correlation, dependency, control, ownership and causation.

new_project_rules.proposal: Replace vague confidence with a multi-axis model status.
new_project_rules.finding: Two theories can have equal overall confidence but very different weaknesses; the vector makes those weaknesses visible.

sequence: classify source as Tim-primary, archive-derived or external comparator
test or retain as T0-T2 research note
new_project_rules.finding: This lets the project preserve creative insight immediately without confusing timestamped revelation with empirical confirmation.

Generate synthetic logarithmic-spiral points and verify recovery of b under noise against Archimedean alternatives.
Simulate Starchforce storage/release under step, pulse and periodic inputs and estimate tau_K.
Create an HMM notebook using synthetic neural states and verify dwell-time/entropy-rate calculations before touching real human data.

Add Q_model status vectors to the highest-priority theory records.
researcher_note: The project now has enough material to begin a second phase: not only collecting correspondences, but systematically asking which mathematical consequences are forced, which are optional modeling choices, and which observations could distinguish them.
